newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on liquidity injection.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on liquidity injection.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates shrugged upside pressures to close down 100 basis points at 18.00 percent on Wednesday, after the central bank injected liquidity into the market to offset surplus paper, traders said.
"There is excess paper in the market, that is why yesterday's close was at an unrepresentative high rate," a trader said.
Dealers said the central bank had injected liquidity because of the "paper glut", a step rarely taken thus far in 1997.
Banco de Mexico injected liquidity by auctioning two credits for a total of 2.335 billion pesos, at terms of one and two days, which it assigned at 19.82 and 19.85 percent, respectively.
"The market's very need for liquidity and a paper glut led the central bank to auction credits," the trader added.
Another trader said secondary rates were under pressure for much of the session on a weak peso and rising U.S. long bond yields.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.9 centavos weaker at 7.9250/7.9290 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year bonds were meanwhile off 28/32 to yield 6.96 percent when the local money market closed.

Dealers said a sharp 134-basis-point fall in bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to 18.37 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction had also sparked speculation that rates could rise again in the coming days.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 35 basis points at 19.90 percent.
Liquidity of 1.034 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation.
